Good morning. It's Tuesday, September 22nd, and we've got a busy pre-market earnings slate to work through. Let's get into it.

The broad macro backdrop takes a back seat today — this edition is all about company-specific earnings and what they tell us about the consumer and industrial landscape heading into the fall.

Starting with the big mover — Viking Therapeutics is spiking hard in pre-market after reporting positive trial data for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss. That's a major readout, it's competitive with the best numbers we've seen in the space, and the market is reacting accordingly. This is a clean bullish catalyst.

AutoZone beat on FQ4 earnings — $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03 — but the quality here is poor. A 1.45% gross margin tailwind came from tariff refunds, and another 1.05% came from a non-cash LIFO adjustment. Strip those out and the beat essentially disappears. Domestic comps were a real miss — up just 1.6% against expectations of 3.1% — and the operating expense ratio worsened by a full 1.0% year-over-year. Management did say sales linearity improved in the back half of the quarter and they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027, but this is a mixed-to-cautious read.

MillerKnoll is a better story on earnings quality. They beat FQ1 EPS by a wide margin — 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents — and even backing out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, they still came in at 42 cents, well above consensus. Orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. The negative is on sales, which fell 3.3% organically and missed estimates, and full-year revenue guidance was trimmed slightly. EPS guidance was left unchanged, which provides some comfort.

THOR Industries missed, and the tone from management was cautious. EPS came in at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 2.3% year-over-year to 12.4%. Management called out stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation squeezing household budgets. Formal fiscal 2027 guidance won't come until later in the fall. The one bright spot — North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year — but the headline read here is bearish.

Cognex announced a roughly $606 million acquisition of RealSense, the leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI. RealSense is growing revenue more than 50% year-over-year, and this deal puts Cognex squarely in the robotics and Physical AI pipeline. Strategically bullish.

Pentair named a new CFO — Bob Hau, effective November 1st. He's got a strong pedigree with prior CFO roles at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. Clean management transition, no financial surprise attached.

Bottom line for the session — VKTX is the high-conviction long catalyst today. Elsewhere, earnings quality is the key filter. Don't chase beats that are tariff-driven. Stay disciplined.
